title: Tenant pin migration: execution template and operator runbook
content:
Purpose:
This is an execution-focused template for migrating a customer (single tenant) from soft-routing to a hard region pin. Goal: ensure auditable steps, minimum downtime for customer traffic, telemetry gates to validate locality, and clear rollback criteria. Not a policy doc — this is what operators and solutions engineers run during a migration.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to single-tenant migrations to a pinned region (customer requests region residency or contract requires it).
- Assumes customer metadata already has target-region and legal acceptance recorded (see linked artifacts).
- Networking (VPC peering, routes) provisioned ahead of time by infra team; this template covers service-level migration and verification.
- Some steps require coordination with CS and Legal for comms windows.

High-level migration phases:
1) Pre-migration validation (T-72h to T-2h)
   - Confirm contract clause and residency scope (data at rest and processing) in ticket PD-1124.
   - Confirm infra readiness: target host pool healthy, autoscaling policy attached, KMS key available in region. Ticket: infra-greenlight.
   - Export current routing snapshot: list of active routes for tenant, active model variants, and KV cache status. Save to artifacts/route-snapshots/<tenant>-<date>.json
   - Create migration-run Jira issue from template (include planned window, rollback owner, SRE pager).
   - Customer comms: draft email in CS template; offer 1-hr window options.

2) Dry-run (T-48h to T-2h)
   - Run routing simulator (local) against a copy of route rules to estimate percent of traffic that would be routed to target region if pin applied. Record expected fallbacks.
   - Telemetry smoke: run a synthetic traffic set through pinned routing in staging; measure latency delta, error rates, and model fallback ratios.
   - Validate billing/billing-tags mapping for pinned region. Ensure tagging is present for cost attribution.

3) Migration window (T+0 to T+2h) — operator steps
   - Step 0: Notify on-call (SRE) and CS Slack channel with migration-run issue link.
   - Step 1: Freeze non-essential deploys for affected services for duration of window.
   - Step 2: Apply pin: create a new routing rule with priority > existing (Rule name: pin-<tenant>-<ts>). Make it conservative: only pin 10% traffic initially if customer agreed to progressive rollout; otherwise 100% if contract requires immediate enforcement.
     - Command (console): POST /admin/routing/rules {"tenant": "<id>", "target_region": "eu-west-1", "weight": 100, "priority": 8000}
     - Command (cli): infractl routing apply --tenant <id> --region eu-west-1 --weight 100 --priority 8000
   - Step 3: Wait 2 minutes for cache propagation. Monitor: route-change propagation metric, routing-error-rate.
   - Step 4: K/V cache warmup: prefetch top-10 prompts via synthetic calls in target region to reduce cold-start latency.
   - Step 5: Validate proxied requests reach target region (sample 1-in-500 requests): check request.trace.region == eu-west-1 and request.tenant == <id>.

4) Telemetry gating (first 30–60 min)
   - Required metrics and gates (thresholds are conservative):
     - Error rate (5xx) for tenant: must not increase by >0.5 percentage points vs baseline.
     - Per-request 95th latency: must not increase by >120ms vs baseline for text generation and embeddings routes.
     - Model fallback rate: <2% additional fallbacks compared to baseline.
     - Downstream infra errors (VGPU OOM, pod crashloop): none beyond expected background noise.
   - If any gate fails: immediately trigger rollback (see rollback section), notify SRE, CS, and escalate to on-call infra lead.

5) Post-migration verification (T+2h to T+48h)
   - Run daily audits for 7 days: sample traffic and confirm region assignment matches pin. Store audit artifacts: audit/<tenant>/<date>.csv
   - Billing verification: confirm cost tags flowing to billing export for region.
   - Data-at-rest verification: verify blobs/objects have correct storage class and KMS region.
   - Legal confirmation: CS confirms customer review completed and acceptance logged.

Rollback plan
   - Criteria for rollback: gate thresholds breached, sustained tail-latency regression >250ms, or customer reports functional break.
   - Rollback action: remove or disable the pin routing rule (priority-based).
     - Command: infractl routing remove --rule pin-<tenant>-<ts> OR set weight back to 0.
   - Post-rollback: clear synthetic warmup, flush KV caches in target region for tenant, reopen site-wide deployment freeze only if caused by migration.
   - Timeline: aim for rollback completion within 10 minutes of decision. Notify customer immediately.

Operator checklist (quick)
   - [ ] Confirm infra-greenlight ticket done
   - [ ] Migration-run Jira issued and assigned
   - [ ] Customer comms scheduled
   - [ ] Backup route snapshot saved
   - [ ] On-call and SRE notified in Slack
   - [ ] Pin rule applied
   - [ ] Telemetry gates green for initial 60 minutes
   - [ ] Post-migration audits scheduled

Customer comms snippets (to use/edit)
   - Pre-window: "We will apply a regional pin for your tenant to ensure data residency in eu-west-1 during the maintenance window on DATE. Expect <x> minute disruption to in-flight requests. Contact: cs@redwood.com."
   - Post-success: "Pin completed. All new requests are being served from eu-west-1. We will run audits for 7 days and share a summary."
   - Post-rollback: "We temporarily rolled back the region-change due to observed regressions. We're investigating and will propose next steps."

Audit artifact list (minimum)
   - route-snapshot-<tenant>-pre.json
   - route-snapshot-<tenant>-post.json
   - telemetry-samples-<tenant>-<ts>.ndjson (sampled traces)
   - audit/<tenant>/<date>.csv (region assignment per sample)
   - cust-comms/<tenant>/<date>-email-thread.pdf

Open questions / TODOs
   - Legal: do we need an explicit signed addendum for progressive 10% rollouts? (Priya)
   - CS asks: how to display pin status in Console UI for customers (UI story PD-1302).
   - Operations: automate route-snapshot creation at rule apply time (ticket: infra-automation).
   - Risk: can a pinned tenant still cause cross-region KV read-throughs in shared caches? Need SRE validation.

Post-mortem triggers
   - Any unexpected customer downtime >5 minutes during migration window.
   - Any audit misalignment (sample shows >1% of traffic outside pinned region after 24h).

Appendix: quick command cheatsheet
   - List rules: infractl routing list --tenant <id>
   - Apply pin: infractl routing apply --tenant <id> --region eu-west-1 --weight 100 --priority 8000
   - Disable pin: infractl routing set-weight --rule pin-<tenant>-<ts> --weight 0
   - Snapshot routes: infractl routing snapshot --tenant <id> --out artifacts/route-snapshot-<tenant>-<ts>.json

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the initial pin rule priority isolated so it never collides with canary rollouts.
- For customers with strict audit windows, pre-generate the audit CSV and share read-only link immediately post-migration.
- If we see repeated rollbacks for similar infra profiles, add an automated preflight that simulates KV behavior for that infra profile.

References and examples: attach these artifacts to the Jira run: CON-templates/migration-email, infra/pinning-sim-run-2024-09-21, billing-tagging-checklist-v1

Last updated by Ava Martinez — comments welcome in the Jira PD-1124 thread.
